title: CLI experiments quicklog - Claire Morgan
content:
Purpose: tiny, command-line-focused run tracker for ad-hoc latency/cost experiments. Keep it short, capture the run command, env, quick metrics, first-draft observations and next steps.

HOW I USE THIS
- Run experiments directly from laptop / dev box with same CLI flags used by CI.
- Copy a row into a proper sheet if results matter.
- Use this as my ephemeral memory for follow-ups.

RUN LOG (most recent top)
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| date       | cmd shorthand        | model    | batch | seq | p50 ms | p95 ms | tok/s | cost/1k toks | notes (short)           |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 2025-02-12 | cls-run-llama2:1      | llama2-13B | 4     | 512 | 122    | 298    | 410   | $0.18        | kv-cache warm, jitter on run 3 |
| 2025-02-11 | quant-eval-pt-8bit    | gpt-open-7B | 8     | 256 | 68     | 142    | 930   | $0.09        | quantized config A, small quality drop |
| 2025-02-05 | burst-batch-check     | redwood-prod | 16    | 128 | 34     | 78     | 1600  | $0.05        | autoscaler kicked in twice |
| 2025-01-20 | cli-latency-smoke     | gpt-open-3B  | 2     | 1024| 210    | 560    | 210   | $0.06        | long seq penalty, consider chunking |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+

ENV SNAPSHOT (for each run above, shorthand):
- CPU: i7-1165G7 laptop for quick runs (local dev).
- GPU: a100-40GB (when noted in cmd).
- Runtime: rwinfer/2.3.1 (local build) + python 3.11.
- CLI: redwoodctl infer --model {model} --batch {batch} --seq {seq} --quant {opt}

RECENT COMMAND EXAMPLES (copy/paste)
- redwoodctl infer --model llama2-13B --batch 4 --seq 512 --kv-cache --profile=quick
- redwoodctl infer --model gpt-open-7B --batch 8 --seq 256 --quant=pt-8bit --timeout 30s
- RWINFER_OPTS="BATCH_TIMEOUT=12ms" redwoodctl infer --model redwood-prod --batch 16 --seq 128 --profile=burst

QUICK OBSERVATIONS / NOTES TO SELF
- p95 spikes often line up with garbage-collection on local runtime. Add GC trace flag next session.
- KV-cache warmup cut p50 by ~40ms for llama2-13B on batch=4. Good for interactive paths.
- Quantization pt-8bit (config A) gives 10-18% speedup, but some hallucination on structured output tests. Add a small eval sweep.
- Autoscaler thresholds look aggressive for short bursts; need to test scale-down latency impact.

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS
- Why did run 2025-02-12 see two distinct p95 modes (one ~170ms, one ~290ms)? hypothesis: background sync + fallback to CPU. Reproduce with --no-sync.
- Is the cost estimate per 1k tokens correct for local GPU accounting? double-check accounting script (scripts/cost_calc.py).

NEXT ACTIONS (prioritized)
- [ ] Re-run 2025-02-12 with GC trace and --no-sync to isolate p95 mode. (owner: Claire)
- [ ] Small eval: quant-config-A vs config-B on 200 eval prompts. (owner: Ravi)
- [ ] Add a minimal, shareable gist with the exact redwoodctl command for bursted runs. (owner: Claire)
- [ ] If p95 wobble reproduces in CI, open ticket (JIRA-2345) with annotated flamegraph.

SNIPPET: quick bash loop I use for micro-benching
for b in 1 2 4 8 16; do 
  RWINFER_PROFILE=dev redwoodctl infer --model gpt-open-7B --batch $b --seq 256 --stat | tee stats-$b.txt; 
  sleep 6; 
done

NOTES TO FUTURE ME:
- This is intentionally terse. If a run looks interesting, migrate to a proper spreadsheet with links to traces and audio.
- Keep the CLI flags consistent between local and CI; put the canonical flags in /runbooks/cli-presets.md

END OF PAGE (ephemeral mini-sheet)
